for applicable positions, ICC would calculate deliver and receive obligations, as set out in paragraphs (a)(i) through (v), for applicable triparty accounts on a net basis. In contrast, Rule 2303 governs Triparty Settlement Obligations subject to gross triparty settlement. Rule 2303(c) describes how ICC would calculate Triparty Settlement Obligations with respect to Settling Open Positions subject to gross triparty settlement in paragraphs (c)(i) through (iii). The difference in drafting between Rule 2302(a) and 2303(c) reflects the distinction between net triparty settlement and gross triparty settlement. ICC would determine if a transaction is subject to net or gross triparty settlement based on the instrument transaction type as set out in Chapter 30 of the Rules and the terms submitted for clearing. For open positions subject to gross triparty settlement, ICC maintains a record associating each such position with the offsetting counter position and Original Counterparty. Treasury Participants and Non-Participant Parties, as applicable, would be required to maintain separate Triparty Settlement Accounts for each house origin or Non-Participant Party portfolio for each counterparty pairing (a “Counterparty Relationship”) subject to gross triparty settlement. ICC would calculate deliver and receive obligations based on positions subject to gross triparty settlement on a gross basis per Counterparty Relationship. Rule 2303(c)(iii) further clarifies that ICC will not net a deliver obligation for one Counterparty Relationship against a receive obligation for another.
Rule 2304 establishes the mechanics applicable to Triparty Settlement Obligations, which are structured in two
(
printed page 74623)
“legs”, through facilities operated by the Triparty Bank (“Triparty Facilities”). Under Triparty Settlement Leg 1, the Delivering Party delivers securities to the ICC Triparty Settlement Account and receives the applicable repurchase price from ICC. Under Triparty Settlement Leg 2, ICC delivers securities to the Receiving Party and receives the corresponding amount. This Rule also permits, with consent from ICC and the relevant Treasury Participant, the use of Individual Client Triparty Settlement Accounts for Non-Participant Parties for standard triparty settlement, and clarifies that ICC bears no responsibility for any default, failure, delay or unavailability affecting the Triparty Bank or Triparty Facilities.
Rules 2305 and 2306 set out provisions that apply in the case of a failure to perform a Triparty Settlement Leg. Treasury Rule 2305 addresses a Triparty Delivery Deficiency, which occurs when a Delivering Party fails to transfer required securities under Triparty Settlement Leg 1, and sets out the actions that ICC may take in response. These actions are set out in paragraphs (a)(i) through (vi) and include, among other things, directing the Triparty Bank to allocate available Eligible Triparty Securities toward curing the deficiency, imposing a late fee and requiring the failing party to reimburse ICC for any costs or expenses resulting from the failure. Pursuant to Rule 2305(b), ICC generally has no obligation to acquire any security to satisfy any Triparty Settlement Obligation. Rule 2305(c) also provides that ICC may in its discretion determine to settle the Triparty Settlement Leg 2 notwithstanding the failure by the Delivering Party, in which case the Delivering Party must pay ICC any losses, costs or expenses incurred in such settlement. Pursuant to Rule 2305(c), ICC may acquire or borrow the relevant securities at a price and on such terms as it determines appropriate. Rule 2306 addresses a Triparty Settlement Payment Failure, which occurs when a Receiving Party fails to make the required payment under Triparty Settlement Leg 2, and sets out the actions that ICC may take in response. These actions are set out in further detail in paragraphs (a)(i) and (ii) and include, among other things, determining to settle Triparty Settlement Leg 1 notwithstanding the failure (in which case the Receiving Party must pay ICC any losses, costs or expenses incurred in such settlement) or terminating the Triparty Settlement Obligation (including both settlement legs thereof) and providing for cash settlement in lieu thereof. In case of a failure by a Delivering or Receiving Party, ICC retains the right to determine that the relevant party (or its Treasury Participant) is in Default and exercise its default remedies under the Rules.
ICC proposes new Chapter 24, titled “Fund Model Triparty Settlement,” which applies only to transactions involving Covered Money Funds under the Money Fund Margin Model as described above and provides for triparty settlement of relevant delivery and receive obligations through a designated Triparty Bank. Rule 2401 introduces relevant definitions, including Covered Money Fund Settlement Account, which refers to the Money Fund Custodial Account established at the Triparty Bank for direct settlement, and the Fund Model Settlement Account, which includes any of the Covered Money Fund Settlement Account or the CP House, CP Client, or Individual Client Triparty Settlement Accounts.
Rule 2402 sets out the calculation of Fund Model Settlement Obligations. To facilitate this calculation, ICC would maintain a record associating each open position in an Eligible Money Fund Transaction with its offsetting counter position and Original Counterparty. Further, each Covered Money Fund would maintain a single Covered Money Fund Settlement Account with separate sub-accounts for each Original Counterparty (a “Money Fund Counterparty Relationship”). ICC would calculate Fund Model Settlement Obligations with respect to Settling Open Positions subject to Fund Model triparty settlement for each Money Fund Counterparty Relationship for applicable Eligible Triparty Securities, as detailed in Rule 2402(c). ICC would not net any delivery obligation in respect of a Fund Model Settlement Obligation against any receive obligation. This is consistent with the design of the Fund Model and preserves the association between positions in Eligible Money Fund Transactions, their offsetting counter positions and Original Counterparties, as well as the separate sub-account structure maintained for each Original Counterparty. Unlike Rule 2303(e), Rule 2402(e) provides that ICC makes determinations in Rule 2402 following the close of business on the preceding ICE Business Day and does not provide that determinations may be made on a same-day settlement basis. This is because, under the Fund Model, the initial leg is not settled through ICC.
Rule 2403 governs the settlement of Fund Model Settlement Obligations and generally follows the triparty settlement framework proposed in Chapter 23. A Fund Model Settlement Obligation in securities between two Fund Model Settlement Accounts would require the Delivering Party to deliver securities to the Receiving Party, and the Receiving Party would pay the applicable repurchase price to the Delivering Party (the “Fund Model Settlement Payment”) through the Triparty Facilities. Fund Model Settlement would occur directly between the Delivering Party's and Receiving Party's accounts at the Triparty Bank (and not through an account of ICC). Rule 2403 also specifies the responsibility for settlement obligations among Treasury Participants and Covered Money Funds. Under this Rule, ICC has no responsibility for any default, failure, delay, or unavailability by or affecting the Triparty Bank or Triparty Facilities.
Rule 2405 addresses Triparty Settlement Payment Failure under the Fund Model. Pursuant to paragraph (a), where the Original Counterparty, as Receiving Party, fails to pay the Fund Model Settlement Payment by the deadline (a “Triparty Settlement Payment Failure”), ICC may determine to proceed with settlement notwithstanding the failure, in which case the Receiving Party would be obligated to pay ICC for any resulting losses, costs and expenses. This provision would not apply if ICC had otherwise determined the Receiving Party or its Treasury Participant in default, in which case the default provisions of Rule 411 as described above or other applicable ICC default rules would apply instead.

Treasury Risk Documentation
ICC's risk management practices for the Treasury Clearing Service are documented in various policies and procedures, including the IM Approach Model Description, the GF and Stress Test Approach Model Description, and Risk Parameter Policy. The IM Approach Model Description sets forth the quantitative risk models and associated methods and techniques used to estimate IM requirements for cleared portfolios of Treasury-related instruments. The GF and Stress Test Approach Model Description describes the general stress testing framework for GF computations developed by ICC for the Treasury Clearing Service and used for financial resources modeling and GF design. The Risk Parameter Policy describes the process of setting and reviewing the risk management model core parameters and their underlying assumptions for the Treasury Clearing Service, as described in the IM Approach Model Description and the GF and Stress Test Approach Model Description.

The proposed rule change would facilitate participation in ICC's Treasury Clearing Service by establishing clear and transparent terms for the clearing of contracts, including repo contracts. The proposed changes facilitate the clearing of such contracts by amending the Rules to (i) update and clarify the rules for Variation Payments, (ii) introduce a new margin model for eligible money funds to facilitate participation by such funds in the Treasury Clearing Service, (iii) expand the rules governing Treasury

The proposed changes to the Treasury Risk Documentation provide further detail on ICC's risk management approach for repo contracts and make clarifications throughout the documentation, thereby extending ICC's risk management documentation to address the risks presented by repo contracts and ensuring that such documentation remains clear and transparent. The proposed rule change would also facilitate access for registered funds to participate in the Treasury Clearing Service by accommodating applicable regulatory requirements for registered funds through the introduction of the Money Fund Margin Model. Taken together, the proposed changes ensure that the Treasury Rules and Treasury Risk Documentation remain effective, up-to-date and transparent, thereby supporting ICC's ability to continue to maintain clear and comprehensive rules and procedures that provide sufficient information to market participants and promoting the prompt and accurate clearance and settlement of securities transactions and protecting investors and the public interest, within the meaning of Section 17A(b)(3)(F) of the Act.

Rule 17ad-22(e)(18)(iv)(C)
[
42
]
requires, in part, that when the covered clearing agency provides central counterparty services for transactions in Treasury securities, it establish objective, risk-based, and publicly disclosed criteria for participation, which ensure that it has appropriate means to facilitate access to clearance and settlement services of all eligible secondary market transactions in Treasury securities, including those of indirect participants. ICC believes that the proposed changes facilitate access to its Treasury Clearing Service by accommodating applicable regulatory requirements for registered funds. ICC designed the Money Fund Margin Model to be consistent with applicable regulatory requirements for registered funds under the Investment Company Act of 1940,
[
43
]
including the full collateralization requirements and existing market practices for repos by registered funds pursuant to Rule 5b-3.
[
44
]
As such, ICC believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the requirements of Rule 17ad-22(e)(18)(iv)(C).
[
45
]
Rule 17ad-22(e)(19)
[
46
]
under the Act requires that each covered clearing agency establish, implement, maintain and enforce written policies and procedures reasonably designed to identify, monitor, and manage the material risks to the covered clearing agency arising from arrangements in which firms that are indirect participants in the covered clearing agency rely on the services provided by direct participants to access the covered clearing agency's payment, clearing, or settlement facilities. The proposed Money Fund Margin Model in Rule 411 would address the indirect participation of eligible money funds in the Treasury Clearing Service, providing ICC with a clear framework to identify, monitor, and manage any associated risks. In particular, Rule 411(c) through (l) would set out additional legal, risk, operational, and default management provisions applicable to the Money Fund Margin Model, which provide, among other things, a first priority lien and security interest granted by each Covered Money Fund to ICC as well as default management actions to be taken by relevant parties. As such, ICC believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the requirements of Rule 17ad-22(e)(19).
[
47
]
(B) Clearing Agency's Statement on Burden on Competition
ICC does not believe the proposed rule change would have any impact, or impose any burden, on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed changes to the Treasury Rules and Treasury Risk Documentation will apply uniformly across all market participants. Certain proposed changes, including amendments to establish the Money Fund Margin Model, are intended to facilitate access to clearing by money funds and thus expand access to clearing for a broader range of market participants. ICC does not believe the proposed amendments would adversely affect the costs of clearing or the ability of market participants to access clearing. Therefore, ICC does not believe the proposed rule change would impose any burden on competition that is inappropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
(C) Clearing Agency's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants or Others
Written comments relating to the proposed rule change have not been received. ICC will notify the Commission of any written comments received by ICC.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
Within 45 days of the date of publication of this notice in the
Federal Register
or within such longer period up to 90 days (i) as the Commission may designate if it finds such longer period to be appropriate and publishes its reasons for so finding or (ii) as to which the self-regulatory organization consents, the Commission will:
(A) by order approve or disapprove such proposed rule change, or
(B) institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule change should be disapproved.
(IV) Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views, and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-ICC-2026-011  on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to File Number SR-ICC-2026-011. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
http://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of such filings will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of ICE Clear Credit and on ICE Clear Credit's website at
https://www.ice.com/​clear-credit/​regulation
.
Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to File Number SR-ICC-2026-011 and should be submitted on or before December 10, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
48
]
Vanessa A. Countryman,
Secretary.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Texas Stock Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change Amending its Fee Schedule, Amending Certain Definitions, and Adding Notes to the Lead Market Maker Program
full_text:

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106905; File No. SR-TXSE-2026-049]
November 16, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on November 10, 2026, Texas Stock Exchange LLC (“TXSE” or “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC” or “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III, below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to: (i) increase the rebate provided for orders that add displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00; (ii) increase the fee for orders that add or remove non-displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00; (iii) reduce the fee for orders that add or remove non-displayed liquidity in securities priced below $1.00; (iv) introduce an enhanced rebate designed to incentivize displayed liquidity in TXSE-listed corporate securities; and (v) amend certain definitions and add notes to the Lead Market Maker Program The text of the proposed rule change is available on the Commission's website (
https://www.sec/​gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
) at the Exchange's website (
https://www.txse.com/​reuglations/​rules-filings
), and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the self-regulatory organization included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below.
(
printed page 74634)
The self-regulatory organization has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend Section A (Transaction Fees) and Section F (Lead Market Maker Program) of the TXSE Fee Schedule to: (i) increase the rebate provided for orders that add displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00; (ii) increase the fee for orders that add or remove non-displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00; (iii) reduce the fee for orders that add or remove non-displayed liquidity in securities priced below $1.00; (iv) introduce an enhanced rebate designed to incentivize displayed liquidity in TXSE-listed corporate securities; and (v) amend certain definitions and add notes to the Lead Market Maker Program. The Exchange proposes to implement these changes effective on November 2, 2026.
[
3
]
The Exchange's Fee Schedule sets forth the standard rebates and fees applied per share for orders that add and remove liquidity, respectively. Currently, TXSE provides a rebate of $0.0031 per share for orders priced at or above $1.00 that add displayed liquidity to the Exchange and charges a fee of $0.0030 per share for orders that remove displayed liquidity from the Exchange.
[
4
]
For securities priced below $1.00, the Exchange provides a rebate of 0.15% of total dollar value (“TDV”) for orders that add displayed liquidity to the Exchange and charges a fee of 0.15% of TDV for orders that remove displayed liquidity from the Exchange.
[
5
]
The Exchange currently charges a fee of $0.0002 per share for orders that add non-displayed liquidity to the Exchange or remove non-displayed liquidity from the Exchange in securities priced at or above $1.00. The Exchange currently charges a fee of 0.05% of TDV for orders that add non-displayed liquidity to the Exchange or remove non-displayed liquidity from the Exchange in securities priced below $1.00.
Base Rates
The Exchange now proposes to amend its base rates applicable to orders that add displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00. The proposed rebate for orders that add displayed liquidity to the Exchange is $0.0032 per share, an increase of $0.0001 from the current rate of $0.0031 per share. In addition, the Exchange proposes to amend its base rates applicable to orders that add or remove non-displayed liquidity in both securities priced at or above $1.00 and securities priced below $1.00. For orders that add or remove non-displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00, the Exchange proposes to charge a fee of $0.0006, an increase of $0.0004 from its current rate of $0.0002 per share. For orders that add or remove non-displayed liquidity in securities priced below $1.00, the Exchange proposes to make these executions free.
The purpose of revising the rates associated with adding and removing displayed and non-displayed liquidity is for business and competitive reasons, as the proposed change is intended to incentivize Members
[
6
]
to submit displayed liquidity to the Exchange by providing a higher rebate for displayed orders that add liquidity to the Exchange and charging a higher fee for non-displayed orders that add liquidity to the Exchange or remove liquidity from the Exchange in securities priced at or above $1.00. The Exchange notes that its proposed base rebate for orders that add liquidity to the Exchange in securities priced at or above $1.00 would remain significantly higher than the base rebates provided by competitors for orders that add displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00.
[
7
]
The Exchange notes that its proposed fee for orders that add non-displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00 is similar to at least one competitor.
[
8
]
The Exchange's proposed fee for orders that remove non-displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00 would remain lower than the fees assessed by competitors for orders that remove non-displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00.
[
9
]
The Exchange's proposal to make executions free in all non-displayed orders that add liquidity to the Exchange in securities priced below $1.00 aligns with the pricing that competitors offer for similar executions.
[
10
]
In addition, the Exchange's proposal to make executions free in all orders that remove non-displayed liquidity in securities priced below $1.00 differs from competitors in that many competitors assess a fee for non-displayed orders that remove liquidity.
[
11
]
In totality, the Exchange believes its proposed fee structure is appropriate in furthering its goal of encouraging Members to submit displayed liquidity to the Exchange as it provides a competitive rebate to Members who add displayed liquidity to the Exchange and charges a fee to those Members who either remove displayed liquidity in all securities or who add or remove non-displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00.
Displayed Liquidity Enhanced Rebate
The Exchange next proposes to introduce an enhanced rebate designed to incentivize quoting in TXSE-listed corporate securities. The Exchange proposes to provide an enhanced rebate of $0.0038 per share in securities priced at or above $1.00 to Members that add displayed liquidity in a TXSE-listed corporate security. The enhanced rebate would not apply to securities priced below $1.00.
The proposed enhanced rebate is designed to encourage Members to submit displayed liquidity to the Exchange in TXSE-listed corporate securities, which contributes to a deeper, more liquid market and provides additional execution opportunities for active market participants. By offering enhanced rebate opportunities to incentivize increased liquidity provision, the
(
printed page 74635)
Exchange seeks to encourage greater trading activity and additional execution opportunities for Members, thereby promoting more robust price discovery and improving overall market quality for all market participants.
Lead Market Maker Program
The Exchange next proposes edits to certain definitions found within Section F (Lead Market Maker Program) of the Fee Schedule. The Exchange introduced its Lead Market Maker (“LMM”) Program in September 2026.
[
12
]
The Exchange's LMM Program offers daily stipends paid by the Exchange to LMMs that achieve certain Minimum Performance Standards
[
13
]
in TXSE-listed symbols. The Exchange now proposes to amend the definition of “Size Near the Inside” and “Time at NBBO” to more accurately reflect the Exchange's calculation of those criteria. “Size Near the Inside” is currently defined as “. . .the average notional depth within 25 basis points of the NBBO.”
[
14
]
The Exchange proposes to revise the definition of “Size Near the Inside” to state “. . .the minimum notional value of both bids and offers within 0.25% of the NBBO for at least 95% of the trading day.” The Exchange notes that this change will continue to measure notional depth relative to the NBBO, but would require the LMM to have a notional depth within 0.25% of each of the NBB and NBO for 95% of the trading day rather than looking at an average of total depth within 25 basis points of the NBBO. The Exchange notes that each of the Signature, Premier, and Core Tiers on the current Fee Schedule indicates the minimum notional value that must be provided on each side of the NBB and NBO.
[
15
]
The addition of the 95% threshold is intended to align the calculation of “Size Near the Inside” with the calculation of “Layered Depth”
[
16
]
and is generally in-line with similar criteria of competitor exchange LMM programs.
[
17
]
“Time at NBBO” is currently defined as “. . .the percentage of time during Regular Trading Hours
[
18
]
in which the LMM maintains both a bid and offer at the NBBO with at least $10,000 notional at each of the NBB and NBO.”
[
19
]
The Exchange proposes to revise the definition of “Time at NBBO” to state “. . .the average of (a) the percentage of time the LMM has at least $10,000 notional at the NBB and (b) the percentage of time the LMM has at least $10,000 notional at the NBO.” This change is designed to account for situations where an LMM may have a valid business reason for quoting the NBB or NBO with the required notional value at different times throughout a trading day. For instance, an LMM's inventory position and exposure to additional purchases or sales may warrant greater participation at the inside market on one side of the NBB or NBO than the other.
[
20
]
Under the current definition of “Time at the NBBO”, an LMM participating at the NBB or NBO without the required notional value throughout Regular Trading Hours would not satisfy the “Time at NBBO” criteria if it did not have the required depth at the NBB and NBO for the requisite amount of time during Regular Trading Hours. Under the proposed definition, however, the Exchange would use the average of the percentage of time that the LMM quoted at each of the NBB and NBO, which would reward LMMs that have valid business cases for having different notional at the NBB and NBO at different times during Regular Trading Hours.
In addition, the Exchange proposes to introduce a “Notes” section to Section F of the Fee Schedule. Under the proposed “Notes” section, the Exchange proposes to add two notes that provide additional clarity to how it performs certain calculations related to the Minimum Performance Standards. First, the Exchange proposes to add the following note: “Periods during which the SIP NBBO is missing, invalid, locked, or crossed are treated as ineligible and excluded from denominators for NBBO-referenced metrics.” Second, the Exchange proposes to add a note stating: “Certain percentage-based thresholds set forth in the Program shall be adjusted for leveraged ETPs to reflect the product's stated leverage factor. The adjusted threshold shall equal the stated threshold multiplied by the absolute value of the leverage factor (
e.g.,
2 for a 2x product, 3 for a 3x product, irrespective of direction). The percentage adjustment applies to the following standards: the basis point threshold of Maximum LMM Spread;
[
21
]
the basis point threshold of Size Near the Inside; the percentage threshold of Layered Depth; the basis point threshold of Opening/Closing Auction Depth;
[
22
]
the basis point threshold of Opening/Closing Auction Reference Price.
[
23
]
Notional dollar thresholds are not
(
printed page 74636)
subject to the leverage adjustment and apply as stated in the applicable tier.” Each of the proposed revisions to the definitions of “Size Near the Inside” and “Time at NBBO” and proposed additions to the proposed “Notes” section is intended to provide additional clarity to LMMs and other market participants regarding how the Minimum Performance Standards are calculated.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the requirements of the Exchange Act. The Exchange believes that the proposed fee changes are consistent with the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act
[
24
]
in that they are designed to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest, and, particularly, are not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers. The Exchange also believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with the provisions of Section 6(b)(4) of the Act,
[
25
]
in that it is designed to provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its Members and other persons using its facilities.
The Exchange operates in a highly competitive market in which market participants can readily direct order flow to competing venues if they deem fee levels at a particular venue to be excessive or incentives to be insufficient. The Exchange believes that its proposed changes reflect a simple and competitive pricing change designed to incentivize market participants to direct their order flow to the Exchange, which the Exchange believes would promote price discovery and price formation and deepen liquidity that is subject to the Exchange's transparency, regulation, and oversight as an exchange, thereby enhancing market quality to the benefit of all Members and investors. The Commission and the courts have repeatedly expressed their preference for competition over regulatory intervention in determining prices, products, and services in the securities markets. In Regulation NMS, while adopting a series of steps to improve the current market model, the Commission highlighted the importance of market forces in determining prices and self-regulatory organization revenues, and also recognized that current regulation of the market system “has been remarkably successful in promoting market competition in its broader forms that are most important to investors and listed companies.”
[
26
]
The proposed changes are intended to attract additional executable interest to the TXSE Book
[
27
]
and encourage Members to compete through displayed quotations. Displayed liquidity informs market participants of available trading interest and contributes to the public price discovery process. Increasing the incentive to display orders, together with providing competitively priced access to those orders, is intended to encourage participation on both sides of a transaction. To the extent these incentives attract additional liquidity, Members seeking executions may benefit from greater available size and additional opportunities to transact, including Members that do not receive an enhanced rebate.
The Exchange competes with other exchanges and off-exchange trading venues for order flow. Members may consider competing venues when evaluating the proposed rates, together with execution quality and other routing considerations. The Exchange believes that the proposed pricing reflects its business judgment concerning the incentives needed to attract order flow and develop its displayed market. The specific relationship between the proposed charges, rebates, and the trading activity they are intended to encourage provides the basis for the Exchange's conclusions concerning reasonableness and equitable treatment, as discussed below.
The Exchange believes that increasing the base rebate for adding displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00 from $0.0031 to $0.0032 per share is reasonable because the additional $0.0001 per share rewards Members for making their trading interest publicly available and exposing that interest to execution. For non-displayed executions in securities priced at or above $1.00, the Exchange proposes to increase the fee for both adding and removing liquidity from $0.0002 to $0.0006 per share. The Exchange believes that this increase is reasonable in light of its objective of encouraging displayed interest. Non-displayed liquidity provides execution opportunities, but does not communicate publicly available trading interest in the same manner as displayed liquidity. The proposed structure therefore assigns a greater financial incentive to orders that contribute directly to displayed price discovery. A Member may continue to use non-displayed orders when confidentiality or other execution considerations warrant paying the applicable fee.
For securities priced below $1.00, eliminating the existing fee of 0.05% of TDV for adding or removing non-displayed liquidity would reduce transaction charges for both participants in the execution. The Exchange believes that eliminating these charges is reasonable because it removes a direct cost of interacting with non-displayed interest in these securities and may encourage additional executions. The distinction between pricing for securities below $1.00 and pricing for securities at or above $1.00 also recognizes that a fixed per-share charge represents a larger proportion of transaction value as a security's price declines. The proposal addresses that concern by charging neither side of a non-displayed execution in securities below $1.00.
The Exchange believes that the proposed base rates are equitably allocated and do not permit unfair discrimination because each rate applies to all Members executing the same category of transaction. The distinctions depend on the security's execution price, whether liquidity is displayed, and whether an order supplies or accesses that liquidity. These characteristics bear a direct relationship to the transaction being priced and the proposal's objectives. The rates do not depend on a Member's identity or business model. In particular, the different treatment of displayed and non-displayed liquidity recognizes the additional public price discovery contribution of displayed interest, while the elimination of sub-dollar non-displayed charges benefits all Members executing those transactions on the same terms.
The Exchange further believes that the proposed enhanced rebate for adding displayed liquidity in TXSE-listed corporate securities is reasonable because it directs enhanced incentives to displayed interest in TXSE-listed corporate securities. The proposed $0.0038 per-share enhanced rebate rewards the addition of displayed
(
printed page 74637)
liquidity, which contributes to a deeper, more liquid market in TXSE-listed corporate securities and provides additional execution opportunities for active market participants. By offering enhanced rebate opportunities to incentivize increased liquidity provision, the Exchange seeks to encourage greater trading activity and additional execution opportunities for Members, thereby promoting more robust price discovery and improving overall market quality for all market participants.. The Exchange notes that while the proposed enhanced rebate is only available for Members that quote in TXSE-listed corporate symbols and is not more broadly available to Members that quote in any name, the Exchange does not believe this is unfairly discriminatory as all Members are eligible to provide quotations in TXSE-listed corporate symbols and the Exchange does not limit this enhanced rebates to Members to register to quote in TXSE-listed corporate symbols. Additionally, Members whose orders do not qualify for the enhanced rebate remain eligible for the applicable base pricing and may benefit from the additional displayed interest the enhanced rebate is intended to attract.
The Exchange believes that encouraging executable displayed interest at competitive prices promotes just and equitable principles of trade and helps perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system by improving the information and trading opportunities available to market participants. Publicly displayed quotations can inform routing and execution decisions by brokers and other intermediaries. In this manner, the proposal supports coordination among persons processing securities information and facilitating securities transactions.
Additionally, the Exchange's proposed amendments to the definitions of “Size Near the Inside” and “Time at NBBO” promotes just and equitable principles of trade, helps perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and contributes to the protection of investors and the public by clarifying the definition so that market participants have a more accurate description of the requirements needed to satisfy the Minimum Performance Standards. The proposed amendments to Section F of the Fee Schedule explain the revised calculations the Exchange would use to determine whether an LMM satisfies the Minimum Performance Standards. The proposed changes to the “Size Near the Inside” definition continue to measure notional size within 0.25% of the NBBO, but replace the average-depth calculation with a minimum-depth requirement that must be met for at least 95% of the trading day, which is similar to the criteria found on competitor exchanges. Similarly, the proposed change to the “Time at NBBO” definition is designed to account for situations where an LMM may have a business justification for not having the requisite notional depth on both the NBB and NBO at the same time during Regular Trading Hours by looking at an average of the percentage of time at each of the NBB and NBO throughout Regular Trading Hours rather than a set percentage at each of the NBB and NBO. The proposed changes are also not unfairly discriminatory as they apply to all LMMs equally, in that all LMMs are subject to the same criteria and calculations when seeking to achieve the daily stipends provided under the LMM Program.
Further, the proposed addition of the “Notes” section to Section F of the Fee Schedule promotes just and equitable principles of trade, helps perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and contributes to the protection of investors and the public because the Exchange believes the proposed notes will provide greater clarity and transparency regarding the calculation and application of certain Minimum Performance Standards under the LMM Program, thereby promoting the consistent and equitable application of such standards to participating LMMs. In particular, including a note about SIP NBBO availability and its application to the calculation of NBBO-referenced metrics promotes a more accurate and consistent assessment of LMM performance, while ensuring that LMMs are not unfairly disadvantaged by market conditions or data irregularities that may be outside their control.
In addition, the Exchange believes its proposal to adjust certain percentage-based performance thresholds for leveraged ETPs based on the absolute value of the product's stated leverage factor is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act because leveraged ETPs are designed to provide returns corresponding to a multiple of the performance of an underlying index or reference asset, which may result in greater price volatility and more pronounced price movements relative to comparable unleveraged products. As such, the Exchange believes that applying identical percentage-based thresholds to leveraged and unleveraged ETPs, without accounting for differences in their respective investment objectives and price characteristics, could impose disproportionately restrictive quoting and liquidity obligations on LMMs assigned to leveraged ETPs. The proposed adjustment is designed to account for these differences by scaling the applicable percentage-based thresholds in proportion to the product's stated leverage factor, thereby establishing performance standards that more appropriately reflect the characteristics of the underlying product. The Exchange also believes that limiting the adjustment to specified percentage-based and basis point thresholds, while maintaining the existing notional dollar thresholds, appropriately balances recognition of the distinct characteristics of leveraged ETPs with the Program's objective of encouraging meaningful liquidity provision. In particular, maintaining the applicable notional dollar thresholds will preserve the existing minimum dollar-denominated liquidity requirements, while the adjustments to the specified percentage-based thresholds will provide LMMs with greater flexibility to accommodate the price characteristics of leveraged products.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
Section 6(b)(8) of the Act
[
28
]
requires that the Exchange's rules not impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purpose of the Exchange Act. The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will result in any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. Rather, as discussed above, the Exchange believes that the proposed fee change would encourage the submission of additional displayed order flow to a public exchange, thereby promoting market depth, execution incentives, and enhanced execution opportunities, as well as price discovery and transparency for all Members. As a result, the Exchange believes that the proposed change furthers the Commission's goal in adopting Regulation NMS of fostering competition among orders, which promotes “more efficient pricing of individual stocks for all types of orders, large and small.”
[
29
]
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intramarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in
(
printed page 74638)
furtherance of the purposes of the Act because the proposed fees and rebates would apply equally to all Members. The proposed fee changes are intended to encourage market participants to add displayed liquidity to the Exchange by increasing the base rebate for adding displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00, increasing the fees for adding and removing non-displayed liquidity in securities priced at or above $1.00, eliminating the fees for adding and removing non-displayed liquidity in securities priced below $1.00, and introducing an enhanced rebate for adding displayed liquidity in TXSE-listed corporate securities priced at or above $1.00, which the Exchange believes will help to encourage Members to send orders to the Exchange to the benefit of all Exchange participants. As the proposed rates are equally applicable to all market participants, the Exchange does not believe there is any burden on intramarket competition. In addition, the Exchange does not believe the proposed amendments to the definitions found within LMM Program and proposed introduction of a “Notes” section under Subsection F of the Fee Schedule will burden competition as these changes are being proposed to provide additional clarity to LMMs and market participants about the calculations used to determine whether an LMM satisfies the Minimum Performance Standards and are not being introduced for competitive reasons.
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intermarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. To the contrary, the Exchange believes that the proposed fee change will increase competition and is intended to draw volume to the Exchange. The Exchange believes that the ever-shifting market share among the exchanges from month to month demonstrates that market participants can shift order flow or reduce use of certain categories of products in response to new or different pricing structures being introduced into the market. Accordingly, competitive forces constrain the Exchange's transaction fees, and market participants can readily trade on competing venues if they deem pricing levels at those other venues to be more favorable. Although this fee change is intended to attract liquidity to the Exchange, most other exchanges in operation today already offer multiple incentives to their participants, including tiered pricing that provides discounted executions, and other exchanges will be able to modify such incentives in order to compete with the Exchange. Accordingly, with respect to a participant deciding to submit an order to remove liquidity, there are multiple exchanges that will continue to be competitively priced for such orders when compared to the Exchange's pricing. Further, while pricing incentives can cause shifts of liquidity between trading centers, market participants make determinations on where to provide liquidity or route orders to take liquidity based on factors other than pricing, including execution quality, technology, functionality, and other considerations. Consequently, the Exchange believes that the degree to which its fees could impose any burden on competition is extremely limited and does not believe that such fees would burden competition of Members or competing venues in a manner that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
The Exchange has neither solicited nor received written comments on the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
30
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(2) thereunder,
[
31
]
because it establishes or changes a due, or fee. At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-TXSE-2026-049 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-TXSE-2026-049. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-TXSE-2026-049 and should be submitted on or before December 10, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
32
]
Vanessa A. Countryman,
Secretary.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend General 4, Rule 1240 To Adopt a New Senior Leader Regulatory Element Interim Program
full_text:

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106911; File No. SR-NASDAQ-2026-098]
November 16, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on November 9, 2026, The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq” or “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC” or “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, and II, below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. Nasdaq has designated the proposed rule change as constituting a “non-controversial” rule change under paragraph (f)(6) of Rule 19b-4 under the Act,
[
3
]
which renders the proposal effective under receipt of this filing by the Commission. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to amend General 4, Rule 1240 (Continuing Education) to adopt new Supplementary Material .03 (Senior Leader Regulatory Element Interim Program) and to harmonize General 4, Rule 1240(a)(6) (Delivery of the Regulatory Element) with recent changes to FINRA Rule 1240.
The text of the proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
https://listingcenter.nasdaq.com/​rulebook/​nasdaq/​rulefilings
,
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The purpose of the proposed rule change is to amend General 4, Rule 1240 (Continuing Education) to adopt new Supplementary Material .03 (Senior Leader Regulatory Element Interim Program) and to make a conforming amendment to General 4, Rule 1240(a)(6) (Delivery of the Regulatory Element) to conform the Exchange's continuing education requirements to recent changes made by the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc. (“FINRA”) to FINRA Rule 1240.
[
4
]
Pursuant to General 4, Rule 1240, registered persons of Exchange members are required to complete continuing education (“CE”) that consists of two mandatory programs, a Regulatory Element and a Firm Element. Regulatory Element CE, which is administered by FINRA, focuses on regulatory requirements and industry standards. Firm Element CE is provided by each member to its registered persons and focuses on the member's securities products, services, and strategies, its policies, and industry trends. The Exchange's Rule 1240 is identical to FINRA Rule 1240, and the Exchange periodically amends its rule to remain harmonized with FINRA's rule.
FINRA has represented that it received a variety of suggestions from member firms and industry groups regarding changes to the Regulatory Element CE requirement for senior leaders (
e.g.,
chief executive officer, chief financial officer), including in response to FINRA Regulatory Notice 25-07.
[
5
]
The Exchange agrees with FINRA that Regulatory Element CE provides individuals with valuable training on recent developments in regulatory requirements and industry standards and, as such, is appropriate for all registered persons, including senior leaders. Senior leaders, however, may realize greater benefit from Regulatory Element CE training that draws from the annual Regulatory Element content but is tailored to their unique roles at a member. Senior leaders may engage with applicable rules differently than frontline representatives and principals because they have broader visibility and responsibilities across their member firm, and, often, its broader organizational structure. Regulatory Element CE content for such leaders therefore may be more effective if it covers the information addressed in the various Regulatory Element CE learning plans but presents the information from a broader, firm-wide perspective, such as firm risks, control systems, approaches to pressure-test firm capabilities and vulnerabilities, and similar enterprise-level considerations.
(
printed page 74658)
Accordingly, the Exchange proposes to adopt Supplementary Material .03 to General 4, Rule 1240 to establish a Senior Leader Regulatory Element Interim Program (“Interim Program”) identical to that adopted and administered by FINRA. A member may elect to have a covered person who is a senior leader satisfy the requirement to complete the Regulatory Element by participating in the Interim Program. For purposes of the Interim Program, the term “senior leader” means any covered person listed on a member's Schedule A of Form BD; any other covered person serving on a member's executive, management or operations committees; or any covered person with similar status or functions who is employed at an affiliate of a member.
[
6
]
Participating senior leaders would continue to be required to take Regulatory Element CE on an annual basis, but the content of the training and the method of delivery would be different.
The Interim Program would be administered in a manner prescribed by FINRA and as set forth in the FINRA Filing, for a period starting on November 2, 2026, and ending on December 31, 2028. The Regulatory Element material for participating covered persons would be developed by FINRA and based on the roles and responsibilities of senior leaders. As described in the FINRA Filing, FINRA would consider the annual learning plan topics assigned to each registration category, but, rather than limiting the content to the specific registration categories the senior leaders hold, the materials would cover content across all registration categories and present significant rule changes, key regulatory developments, and other Regulatory Element topics from the unique organizational vantage point of senior leaders. The materials would remain consistent with the core objectives of Regulatory Element CE.
Under the Interim Program, the chief compliance officer (“CCO”) or other senior compliance officer at a participating member would provide the training to participating senior leaders (including any participating senior leaders of affiliated entities), and would have the discretion to supplement the training materials to provide the most relevant and effective training for the member's senior leaders.
[
7
]
The CCO of a member designated under General 9, Section 21(c)
[
8
]
would provide FINRA with the list of participating senior leaders and represent to FINRA that the senior leaders completed the Regulatory Element material in a manner prescribed by FINRA. Further, a senior leader who participates in the Interim Program would certify that he or she has completed the Regulatory Element material, and the member would retain such certification.
[
9
]
Senior leaders who participate and successfully complete the training would satisfy their annual Regulatory Element requirement under Rule 1240; those who do not participate would be required to complete the Regulatory Element CE courses assigned by FINRA, as they do today.
In connection with the Interim Program, the Exchange also proposes to amend General 4, Rule 1240(a)(6) (Delivery of the Regulatory Element), which currently provides that the Regulatory Element shall be administered through Web-based delivery or such other technological manner and format as specified by the Exchange. The Exchange proposes to delete the word “technological” so that the rule would provide that the Regulatory Element shall be administered through Web-based delivery or such other manner and format as specified by the Exchange. This conforming amendment, which mirrors FINRA's amendment to FINRA Rule 1240(a)(6), would permit the CCO or other senior compliance officer at a member participating in the Interim Program to deliver the Regulatory Element training to participating senior leaders.
The Interim Program would be voluntary, and no member would be required to participate. While the Interim Program is in place, FINRA would evaluate demand for the program and whether it is meeting the goals of Regulatory Element CE for senior leaders.
[
10
]
If the Interim Program is not extended or Rule 1240.03, as may be amended, is not approved as permanent by the Commission, Supplementary Material .03 would automatically sunset on December 31, 2028, and covered persons who are senior leaders would not be able to participate in the Interim Program after such date.
Nasdaq has filed the proposed rule change for immediate effectiveness and has requested that the Commission waive the requirement that the proposed rule change not become operative for 30 days after the date of filing so Nasdaq can implement the proposed rule change immediately.
[
11
]
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that its proposal is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
12
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
13
]
in particular, in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. The Exchange also believes the proposal is consistent with Section 6(c)(3) of the Act,
[
14
]
which authorizes the Exchange to prescribe standards of training, experience and competence for persons associated with Exchange members.
The proposed rule change continues the Exchange's commitment to Regulatory Element CE while providing appropriate flexibility for members and senior leaders, and maintains the requirement that all registered persons complete appropriate Regulatory Element content on an annual basis. Because participation would be voluntary, a member could require its senior leaders to continue to take the Regulatory Element CE assigned for their specific registration categories if the member concludes such training would be more appropriate. Senior leaders would not be exempt from the annual Regulatory Element requirement; only the framing and method of delivery of the training would differ. The ability of a member's CCO or other senior compliance officer to supplement the
(
printed page 74659)
training materials would further help to ensure that the training is particularly effective for the member's senior leaders.
Moreover, the proposed rule change will harmonize the Exchange's continuing education rule with FINRA Rule 1240, thereby promoting consistency in CE requirements across self-regulatory organizations and avoiding the confusion and burden that could arise if dual members were subject to divergent standards. The Exchange believes this harmonization promotes just and equitable principles of trade and protects investors and the public interest.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed rule change is not intended to address competitive issues, but rather to conform the Exchange's continuing education requirements to those of FINRA. The Interim Program is voluntary and would be available equally to all members, which may elect participation based on their own evaluation of the training needs of their senior leaders and may switch senior leaders between the Interim Program and the assigned Regulatory Element CE. Because the Interim Program is voluntary, members are not expected to use it unless they believe it benefits their firms, and any potential unintended impacts would be limited due to the term of the Interim Program.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were either solicited or received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
Because the foregoing proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative for 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, it has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
15
]
and subparagraph (f)(6) of Rule 19b-4 thereunder.
[
16
]
A proposed rule change filed under Rule 19b-4(f)(6) normally does not become operative for 30 days after the date of filing. However, pursuant to Rule 19b-4(f)(6)(iii),
[
17
]
the Commission may designate a shorter time if such action is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. As noted in its Form 19b-4 and above in Item II, Nasdaq has requested that the Commission waive the 30-day delay requirement so that the proposed rule change may become operative immediately upon filing.
More specifically, Nasdaq stated in its request that immediate operability is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest because the Interim Program is a FINRA program that is already in operation. As Nasdaq noted, FINRA's identical Interim Program began on November 2, 2026, and Nasdaq's proposal creates no new program, content or oversight process. Rather, Nasdaq stated that its proposal allows Exchange members to take part, on the same terms as FINRA members, in a program that is already running and that delaying the operative date of the proposal for 30 days would not change how the Interim Program is administered and would serve no investor protection purpose. Nasdaq also claimed that the absence of a waiver here would keep Exchange members, many of which are also FINRA members, out of a program already open to FINRA members and, as a result, would create a period in which Exchange and FINRA continuing education requirements diverge, which could cause confusion and burden for dual members. According to Nasdaq, the waiver would give Exchange members a meaningful opportunity to elect participation, identify eligible senior leaders, and complete necessary planning before the December 31, 2026, Regulatory Element CE deadline, and to begin evaluating participation for the 2027 CE cycle. For these reasons, the Commission believes that waiving the 30-day operative delay for this proposed rule change is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. Accordingly, the Commission hereby waives the 30-day operative delay and designates the proposed rule change operative upon filing.
[
18
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number
SR-NASDAQ-2026-098 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to File Number SR-NASDAQ-2026-098. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to File Number SR-NASDAQ-2026-098 and should be submitted on or before December 10, 2026.
(
printed page 74660)
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
19
]
Vanessa A. Countryman,
Secretary.

November 16, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934
(

(“Act”),

and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2

notice is hereby given that, on November 5, 2026, 24X National Exchange LLC (“24X” or “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the self-regulatory organization. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to make certain amendments to its warrant performance incentive program.
[
3
]
The proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
https://equities.24exchange.com/​regulation
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the self-regulatory organization included statements concerning the purpose of, and basis for, the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of those statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant parts of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and the Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange adopted a warrant performance incentive program (“Program”) to allow Members of the Exchange who participate in the Program (“Participants”)
[
4
]
to earn the right to purchase Non-Voting Common Units
[
5
]
of 24X US Holdings LLC (“24X US Holdco”), the Exchange's parent company.
[
6
]
As described in the Warrant Program Release, each Member of the Exchange may become a Participant in the Program by prepaying $500,000 in Exchange fees (“Prepayment Fee”) and satisfying the Program eligibility requirements.
[
7
]
Upon joining the Program, each Participant will receive a warrant that vests based on the Participant's achievement of certain minimum trading volumes (“Target Volume”)
[
8
]
on the Exchange during each designated pre-determined period in which the Program is in effect (“Measurement Period”)
[
9
]
and the Exchange's achievement of a minimum market share during such Measurement Periods (“24X Minimum Overall Market Share”).
[
10
]
When the warrants vest, Participants will have the right to exercise the warrants to purchase a certain number of 24X US Holdco Non-Voting Common Units.
The Exchange has determined to revise the Program to make additional Non-Voting Common Units available to be purchased by Participants starting in the first Measurement Period of 2027 (“Additional Equity”), under different terms than those applicable to the Non-Voting Common Units currently available to be purchased through the Program (“Original Equity”). Specifically, the right to purchase Additional Equity would extend through two additional Measurement Periods in 2028, would be subject to a reduced Prepayment Fee, and would be based on maker volume only instead of total trading volume.
The Exchange also proposes to make two additional changes to the terms of the Program that would apply to the right to purchase both the Original Equity and the Additional Equity. Specifically, as described below, the Exchange proposes to eliminate the 24X Minimum Overall Market Share threshold requirement and exclude certain dates from the calculation of Target Volume in each Measurement Period. All other aspects of the Program would remain the same as described in the Warrant Program Releases.
[
11
]
a. Proposed Changes With Respect to Additional Equity Only
i. Description and Timing of Additional Equity
The Original Equity consists of 1,098,040 Non-Voting Common Units representing 10% of the outstanding total Units on a fully diluted basis of 24X US Holdco as of September 29, 2025. The Original Equity may be purchased by Participants upon the exercise of warrants that vest in accordance with the Program based on trading that occurs during the Program Period, which begins on and including October 14, 2025 and ends on and including December 31, 2027.
[

]
The Original Equity is allocated among the Measurement Periods for each of the three years of the Program as follows:
